s: Lao Tzŭ teaches non-interference with natural goodness (in answer to Ts'ui Chü)
q: "Be careful," replied Lao Tzŭ, "not to interfere with the natural goodness of the heart of man.

s: human heart can be forced down or stirred up forced down or stirred up (In each case the issue is fatal)
q: Man's heart may be forced down or stirred up. In each case the issue is fatal.

s: Confucianists stand forth to preach (in the midst of gyves and fetters)
q: then the Confucianists and the Mihists, in the midst of gyves and fetters, stood forth to preach!

s: Mihists stand forth to preach (in the midst of gyves and fetters)
q: then the Confucianists and the Mihists, in the midst of gyves and fetters, stood forth to preach!

s: Yellow Emperor is a ruler of the empire (for nineteen years)
q: The Yellow Emperor sat on the throne for nineteen years, and his laws obtained all over the empire.

s: Kuang Ch'êng Tzŭ possesses perfect TAO (as described by the Yellow Emperor)
q: I am told, Sir, that you are in possession of perfect TAO.

s: Spirit of the Clouds is a power unavoidably summoned to govern (because people depend upon its movements)
q: but the people depend upon my movements. I am thus unavoidably summoned to power;

s: Vital Principle teaches inaction (as the means for making the world good)
q: Rest in inaction, and the world will be good of itself.

s: Vital Principle attributes confusion to government (including violation of life's conditions)
q: That the scheme of empire is in confusion," said the Vital Principle, "that the conditions of life are violated, that the will of God does not triumph, that the beasts of the field are disorganised, that the birds of the air cry at night, that blight reaches the trees and herbs, that destruction spreads among creeping things,--this, alas! is the fault of _government_."

s: government causes human dissatisfaction (when it produces excessive happiness or sorrow)
q: Dissatisfaction and discontent are subversive of virtue; and without virtue there is no such thing for an empire as stability.

s: heaven and earth is a relationship out of harmony (according to the Spirit of the Clouds)
q: The relationship of heaven and earth is out of harmony," said the Spirit of the Clouds;

s: God has TAO (the TAO of God is fundamental)
q: There is the TAO of God, and the TAO of man.

s: TAO has fundamental status (as the TAO of God)
q: The TAO of God is fundamental: the TAO of man is accidental.

s: Perfect Man undertakes affairs (without declining them)
q: He undertakes affairs without declining them.

s: Perfect Man accommodates to matter (without ignoring it)
q: He accommodates himself to matter and does not ignore it.

s: the Sage acts through inaction (his action is ultimately inaction)
q: Thus the action of the Sage is after all inaction.

s: the Sage looks up to God (without offering to aid)
q: Therefore the true Sage looks up to God, but does not offer to aid.

s: the Sage guides by TAO (without making plans)
q: He guides himself by Tao, but makes no plans.

s: TAO consists of inaction and compliance (as the TAO of God)
q: Inaction and compliance make the TAO of God: action and entanglement the TAO of man.

s: Inaction is a means of adapting to natural conditions (for a perfect man summoned to power)
q: Therefore, for the perfect man who is unavoidably summoned to power over his fellows, there is naught like _Inaction_.

s: Inaction supports the State (through respect and love for it as one's own body)
q: And so it is that he who respects the State as his own body is fit to support it, and he who loves the State as his own body, is fit to govern it.

s: man has natural dispositions (which should not be perverted)
q: Letting alone springs from fear lest men's natural dispositions be perverted and their virtue laid aside.

s: natural conditions of existence require adaptation
q: By means of inaction he will be able to adapt himself to the natural conditions of existence.

s: Virtue is a condition of stability (for an empire)
q: Dissatisfaction and discontent are subversive of virtue; and without virtue there is no such thing for an empire as stability.

s: THE UNIVERSE is vast vast
q: Vast as is the universe, its phenomena are regular.

s: God is a sovereignty (divine)
q: Sovereignty begins in virtue and ends in God. Therefore it is called divine.

s: Virtue connects God (through man)
q: Thus, virtue was the connecting link between God and man, while TAO spread throughout all creation.

s: Virtue connects man (with God)
q: Thus, virtue was the connecting link between God and man, while TAO spread throughout all creation.

s: Inaction governs the Empire (of old)
q: Of old, the empire was under the sovereignty of inaction. There was the virtue of God,--nothing more.

s: Inaction is a sovereignty (of the empire of old)
q: Of old, the empire was under the sovereignty of inaction. There was the virtue of God,--nothing more.

s: the Empire is under the sovereignty of Inaction (of old)
q: Of old, the empire was under the sovereignty of inaction. There was the virtue of God,--nothing more.

s: the Empire is correct (Words being in accordance with TAO)
q: Words being in accordance with TAO, the sovereignty of the empire was correct.

s: the Empire has clear duties duties (when delimitations accord with TAO)
q: Delimitations being in accordance with TAO, the duties of prince and subject were clear.

s: the Empire has governing officials officials (whose abilities accord with TAO)
q: Abilities being in accordance with TAO, the officials of the empire governed.

s: the Sage dwells like the quail
q: The true Sage dwells like the quail

s: THE UNIVERSE has regular phenomena regular
q: Vast as is the universe, its phenomena are regular.

s: the Sage dwells at random (like the quail)
q: The true Sage dwells like the quail At random.

s: the Sage feeds like a fledgeling
q: The true Sage dwells like the quail At random. and feeds like a fledgeling.

s: the Sage leaves no trace none (when travelling like a bird)
q: He travels like the bird, leaving no trace behind.

s: the Sage cultivates Virtue (in retirement when the empire lacks TAO)
q: If there be not TAO, he cultivates virtue in retirement.

s: the Sage enters the kingdom of God (after a thousand years of this weary world)
q: After a thousand years of this weary world, he mounts aloft, and riding upon the white clouds passes into the kingdom of God

s: the Sage is secure eternity (in the kingdom of God)
q: where he rests secure in eternity.

s: the Sage has complete virtue complete virtue
q: The man of complete virtue remains blankly passive as regards what goes on around him.

s: the Sage is passive blankly passive (regarding what goes on around him)
q: The man of complete virtue remains blankly passive as regards what goes on around him.

s: the Sage is natural as originally by nature
q: He is as originally by nature, and his knowledge extends to the supernatural.

s: the Sage has supernatural knowledge the supernatural
q: He is as originally by nature, and his knowledge extends to the supernatural.

s: THE UNIVERSE has countless contents countless
q: Countless though its contents, the laws which govern these are uniform.

s: the Sage has an expansive heart an enlarged heart (through virtue)
q: Thus, his virtue expands his heart, which goes forth to all who come to take refuge therein.

s: the Sage responds to influences (without initiating movement)
q: His heart does not initiate the movement, but simply responds to an influence brought to bear.

s: the Sage can see light (where all is dark)
q: He can see where all is dark.

s: the Sage can hear harmony (where all is still)
q: He can hear where all is still. In the darkness he alone can see light. In the stillness he alone can detect harmony.

s: man has senses senses (which are his bane)
q: Man's senses his bane--Illustrations.

s: man is controlled by outward circumstances
q: Men were controlled by outward circumstances, applying their in-born skill to the development of civilised life.

s: man has inborn skill skill (applied to civilised life)
q: Men were controlled by outward circumstances, applying their in-born skill to the development of civilised life.

s: all things are informed by TAO
q: TAO spread throughout all creation.

s: all things respond to TAO (when the point of view accords with TAO)
q: The point of view being always in accordance with TAO, all things responded thereto.

s: all things proceed on their course (when the empire does nothing)
q: They did nothing, and all things proceeded on their course.

s: THE UNIVERSE has uniform laws uniform
q: Countless though its contents, the laws which govern these are uniform.

s: Lao Tzŭ is associated with the Record (as its possible speaker or author)
q: Kuo Hsiang says the _Record_ was the name of a work ascribed to Lao Tzŭ.

s: Lao Tzŭ is identified with Confucius (by some commentators)
q: This "Master" has been identified with both Chuang Tzŭ and Lao Tzŭ.

s: Nothing finds the magic pearl (when Intelligence, Sight, and Speech fail)
q: Finally, he employed Nothing, and Nothing got it.
